props.gloss_en: a stew pot and a pot removed [from the fire] boiling -- one may not put spices into them
but one may put [spices] into a bowl or into a tureen
R' Yehuda: one may put [spices] into anything, except something containing vinegar or brine
R' Yehuda's clause refers to the first clause [the boiling pot], and is lenient
or perhaps R' Yehuda's clause refers to the last clause [the bowl and tureen], and is stringent
R' Yehuda says: into all stew pots one puts [spices], into all boiling pots one puts [spices], except something containing vinegar or brine
Rav Yosef thought: salt is like a spice -- in a first vessel it cooks, in a second vessel it does not
R' Chiyya taught: salt is not like a spice
Abaye (first version): 'salt is not like a spice' means that in a second vessel too it cooks
Abaye (second version): 'salt is not like a spice' means that in a first vessel too it does not cook
Rav Nachman: salt needs as much cooking as ox-meat

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע, דתניא: רבי יהודה אומר לכל אילפסין הוא נותן, לכל הקדירות רותחות הוא נותן -- R' Yehuda permits the boiling pots themselves
והיינו דאמר רב נחמן: צריכא מילחא בישולא כבישרא דתורא -- that is what Rav Nachman said

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה אביי: תני רבי חייא, מלח אינה כתבלין -- R' Chiyya taught that salt is not like a spice (the same objection in both versions, 42b.4 and 42b.5)
